newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI sees profit surge - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: India SBI sees profit surge - newspaper.

text.p: The State Bank of India (SBI), the country's largest commercial bank, is expecting a net profit of 13 billion rupees in the financial year 1996/97 (April-March), the Business Standard said on Wednesday.
The newspaper, quoting SBI chairman P.G. Kakodkar, said the figure would imply a slight acceleration in profitability during the second half of the fiscal year.
SBI's net profit for the six months ended September 30, 1996 was 6.4 billion rupees. Net profit in 1995/96 was 8.32 billion rupees.
A two percent cut in the cash reserve ratio has enabled the bank to maintain its high level of profitability, the newspaper said.
SBI's lending portfolio, which grew by 20 billion rupees in the past 11 months, is expected to increase by 10 to 11 percent by March 31 over the previous year, it said.
